title: CSM/Boiler answer re-framed in the Indian authority order - DG Shipping/DGMA statutory, IRS class, IACS UR Z18 unified baseline, ClassNK demoted to implementation example
candidate_claim: Follow-up to CORR-CSM-BOILER-SURVEY-20260823. The base correction was right that the boiler is not an ordinary CSM machinery item, but it reached that answer through IACS UR Z18 and a ClassNK equipment list, with no Indian authority in the chain. For an Indian MEO Class I candidate that is the wrong order, and it risked reading ClassNK's list as universal.
rationale: Verified against the Indian sources the base correction never consulted, and they do not merely re-order the answer - they change part of it. IRS Guidelines on Continuous Surveys of Machinery (IRS-G-SUR-02, March 2022) draws its boiler line as a CHIEF ENGINEER CREDIT boundary, not as a CSM eligibility boundary: section 4 is titled 'Typical List of Machinery Items not acceptable for Survey by Chief Engineers', and 4.1.1(d) lists 'Boilers and all other pressure vessels' among items that 'are to be surveyed by IRS Surveyors'. That is a different proposition from the base correction's flat statement that boilers 'are not CSM items', and for an IRS-classed ship the flat statement is too strong. The defensible claim, which all three layers support, is narrower: the boiler's PRESSURE BOUNDARY is not on the five-year CSM item interval, because its internal examination is governed by the boiler survey regime. The base correction's auxiliary list was also ClassNK's rather than IRS's. IRS section 3.1.1 names (w) forced or induced draught fans and (aa) adjustment of exhaust gas boiler safety valves under steam as Chief-Engineer-surveyable; it does not name boiler burning pumps or feed water pumps, which came from the ClassNK list, and 4.1.1(e) puts boiler fuel oil heaters above 6.9 bar out of the Chief Engineer's reach. Those two pump types have been removed from the card's list and ClassNK's list is now shown as an example of how societies differ, not as the list. On intervals the three layers coincide and the card now says so rather than implying one source: IACS UR Z18 section 2.1, the IRS regime, and the Indian statutory requirement all give a minimum of two internal examinations per five-year special survey cycle with no two more than 36 months apart.
note: The Indian statutory layer is cited for its terminology and its interval, with its status stated honestly. The current draft Merchant Shipping (Survey, Audit and Certification) Rules, 2026 opens with 'DRAFT ... NOTIFICATION ... New Delhi, the____________ 2026 ... G.S.R. ______ (E)' - blank date, blank GSR number - so it is under the Merchant Shipping Act 2025 but not yet notified, and the card says so in the reference box rather than quoting it as binding. What it establishes and what nothing else in the repository carried is the Indian statutory VOCABULARY: the rotational machinery regime is the 'running survey' under Rule 274 of the MS (Construction and Survey of Passenger Ships) Rules 2026, whose schedule the owner draws up and the Administration approves, with the RO keeping a parallel 'Continuous Survey of Hull & Machinery' cycle and the Principal Officer specifying which items need MMD attendance. A candidate who answers 'CSM' to a DG Shipping examiner without knowing the statutory word is 'running survey' is answering in the class register only. The base correction CORR-CSM-BOILER-SURVEY-20260823 is not reopened: 'main boilers' stays out of the machinery list and the false IACS PR 1C citation stays removed. One nuance is recorded and NOT actioned: the card's CE Oral Tip says the Chief Engineer cannot credit 'the Boiler Safety Valves', which is right as a general statement under IRS 4.1.1(d), but IRS 3.1.1(aa) and UR Z18 2.2 both allow the Chief Engineer to set exhaust-gas boiler safety valves at sea where steam cannot be raised in port. Editing examiner-voice CE-tip prose is a separate editorial act and was not bundled here.

authority.source: IRS Guidelines on Continuous Surveys of Machinery, IRS-G-SUR-02, March 2022
clauses: 1.1.2 quoting Main Rules Part 1, Chapter 2, Section 8.2 - at the Owners' request and upon approval, a system of continuous Surveys of Machinery may be undertaken whereby the requirements of Special Survey of machinery are completed within a 5 year period; the interval between consecutive examinations of each item is not to exceed five years

1.1.3 quoting Main Rules Part 1, Chapter 2, Section 1.4 - continuous surveys of a few machinery items may be carried out under the supervision of the Chief Engineer subject to conditions and confirmatory survey by IRS Surveyors
2.2.2 - approximately one-fifth of the machinery items are to be examined each year
3.1.1(w) forced or induced draught fans - acceptable for survey by Chief Engineers
3.1.1(aa) adjustment of exhaust gas boiler safety valves under steam - acceptable for survey by Chief Engineers
4.1.1(d) 'Boilers and all other pressure vessels' - NOT acceptable for survey by Chief Engineers, to be surveyed by IRS Surveyors
4.1.1(e) boiler fuel oil heaters, other than low pressure (less than 6.9 bar) fuel oil heaters - NOT acceptable for survey by Chief Engineers

authority.source: Draft Merchant Shipping (Survey, Audit and Certification) Rules, 2026, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
clauses: 2.3 Running in Surveys - in accordance with Rule 274 of the MS (Construction and Survey of Passenger Ships) Rules 2026, the hull and machinery of any Ship shall be surveyed on the 'running survey' principle and shall be opened up and surveyed within the period of 05 years; the owner draws up the schedule and the Director General approves it
2.3(2) - the Classification Society or Recognized Organization draws up a similar schedule under the 'Continuous Survey of Hull & Machineries' (CSH & M) scheme in a five year cycle
2.3(3) - the MMD specifies items which may require personal attendance of the MMD surveyor; the Principal Officer holds overall responsibility for the running survey regime

2.4 / 5 Boiler Surveys - boilers are required to be surveyed periodically in compliance with SOLAS requirements and the classification society or RO rules; a minimum of two internal examinations during each five-year special survey cycle; the interval between any two such internal examinations shall not exceed 36 months; one internal examination in conjunction with the Initial or renewal Safety Construction Survey and the other with the Intermediate Safety Construction Survey

cards.rationale: Four changes, all inside the boiler/CSM explanation and its references. The Vital Auxiliary Systems bullet now names the boiler auxiliaries IRS actually lists and drops the two pump types that came from ClassNK, and says the approved list differs between societies. The 'Not the boiler itself' bullet is narrowed from 'boilers are not CSM items' to the claim the sources support - the pressure boundary is not on the 5-year CSM interval because the boiler survey regime governs its internal examination. A new bullet sets out the Indian answering order, statutory before class, and gives the statutory word 'running survey'. A second new bullet states the trap the base correction left open: being inside the machinery-survey framework is not the same as being creditable by the Chief Engineer, with IRS 4.1.1(d) as the example. The reference box is re-ordered DG Shipping/DGMA, IRS Main Rules, IRS-G-SUR-02, IACS UR Z18, SOLAS, ClassNK-as-example. Question text, anchor and card position unchanged; no examiner attribution or CE Oral Tip touched. Version badge Q40 v1.1 -> v1.2.

propagation.finding: Cites IACS UR Z7/Z7.1 as governing CMS. UR Z18 is the machinery survey requirement. This refinement's authority work confirms the defect but does not require bundling it: the card's substantive CMS content, including its statement that CMS excludes pressure vessels such as auxiliary boilers, is correct and unaffected. Remains a separate governed correction.

The q40 stem expands CSM as 'Condition Survey Method'. The Indian sources confirm the correct expansion is Continuous Survey of Machinery, and the statutory analogue is the 'running survey'. Not changed here: a question stem drives examiner-index display text and the question-text controls, so it is a separate bounded correction.
Its trap answers 'No. Boilers and pressure vessels are strictly surveyor-only items', which is exactly what IRS 4.1.1(d) says. Strengthened, not contradicted, by the Indian sources.
